discovery: Invention of silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors for precision vertexing of charged particles

nominees.name: Erik H. M. Heijne
nominees.affiliation: CERN, Geneva, Switzerland (and IEAP, Czech Technical University, Prague)

motivation: Starting around 1980, Heijne and colleagues first used planar-processed silicon microstrip detectors in a high-energy experiment. Heijne and Jarron then developed the hybrid pixel detector, which bonds a segmented silicon sensor to a custom CMOS readout chip. Parker pioneered monolithic pixel concepts and 3D-electrode silicon sensors. Together these made it possible to track charged particles with micron precision at high rates and radiation levels. Silicon vertex detectors made b-tagging practical, and b-tagging was essential to the top-quark discovery at the Tevatron and to the Higgs discovery and Higgs-to-bb measurements at the LHC. The same technology is the basis of X-ray imaging detectors used in synchrotron science and medicine, and of the 4D timing trackers planned for future colliders. This invention transformed how particle physics experiments are done.
